The brand recommends using a commercial washer and dryer only for routine care.

It has been revealed that we’ve come to know Brooklinen very well over the years, and several of us have tried and loved their signature down comforter while testing their products. Contributor Rebecca Grambone calls the original “very high quality and luxurious” with “strong hotel bed vibes.”.

Even though the down comforter never disappointed, the brand gave it an upgrade this year, and shopping writer Julia Harrison says it stacks up even better against the old version, citing “some notable upgrades.” For one thing, “they’ve upped the amount of fill in each and cloaked them in a sateen shell for coolness,” Harrison says. “They, thankfully, kept the easy-tie loops, not just in the four corners but the top and bottom as well, which work perfectly with their duvet covers.” The fill power only decreased for the lightweight offering (from 650 to 600), so it’s designed to feel even more cool and breathable if you sleep hot.

Technical stuff aside, Harrison indicates it “feels expensive,” notably from the fluffy and even baffle-box construction and the velvety sateen cover. “It even smells expensive: clean, fresh, unbothered,” she adds. “The feathers never poke out and stab me, which is a real matter with down on occasion, and I’ve had no issue having the cover stay in place.” Harrison has the all-season version to make her life easy (meaning she doesn’t have to switch it out or store it from season to season), and “it’s never too hot or too cold, and it’s easy to fluff up in the morning when I’m making my bed.”.

In a recent development, our team has done a lot of research on Quince over the last year, and we’ve given the much-discussed brand’s linen duvet covers and bamboo sheets our seal of approval for their affordability and durability. So, naturally, we were excited to hear contributor Zoë Sessums’s praise of their goose down comforter. She noted that the price point is surprisingly low for such high-quality bedding (especially compared to competitors), and says she would recommend it to anyone. Filled with European white goose down and available in both lightweight and all-season options, this down duvet insert is designed with double-stitched seams and a baffle-box construction to prevent lumps.

Industry observers note that boll & Branch has cracked the code for breathable, thoughtfully crafted and sustainable bedding. The retailer is conscientious with their approach to supply chain and holistic practices, earning Fair Trade and GOTS seals as well as Oeko-Tex certifications, which means you’re sleeping under something luxe that isn’t packed with microplastics.

Certifications aside, AD PRO senior editor Mel Studach can attest to this: The brand’s down insert has a 100% organic cotton shell that works as a breathable layer strong enough to keep the fills from poking through. “The duvet insert made a great first impression,” Studach notes. “And with attachable corner loops, the insert was easy to situate within my Blu Dot duvet cover. The baffle-box construction keeps the down evenly distributed throughout the cover.” Studach recommends this for a year-round option if you like to keep your room cold and snuggle up. One last perk: The various weight options mean you can better personalize it to your sleep temperature preferences.

Because this is more of a quilt-comforter hybrid, our tester states she typically prefers blankets with a little more loft, or a fluffier feel to them.

According to recent reports, perhaps you prefer a generously sized blanket over a lofty comforter, or maybe you’re looking for a lighter weight bed topper instead of a chunky knit blanket. Whatever the case, senior shopping editor Nashia Baker indicates this is the perfect quilt-comforter hybrid. “I am always looking for some sort of two-in-one design element in my apartment whenever I can: I have a storage bed so I don’t have to conjure up some other place to put all my bulky blankets and clothes, a cooling pillow so I don’t have to crank my AC unless it’s absolutely necessary, you get the gist,” she says. “So the fact that I don’t need to have a separate duvet insert and cover in the mix is nice when I want a more simple bedspread.”.

In a recent development, baker indicates the quilted comforter feels like a hug goodnight. “I genuinely can’t sleep with anything too thin—like just a top sheet—or I’ll wake up in the middle of the night,” she says. “This is the perfect mid-weight blanket to sleep under without overheating (thanks to the cotton gauze-y fabric).” Though colorways switch up through the seasons, we’re partial to the checkered patterns that can instantly add more personality to your bedscape. All of the designs are definitely a step up from the plain white comforters that dominate the market.

Adding both inserts inside a duvet cover can feel heavy and harder to wrangle.

Contributor Yelena Moroz Alpert has had this wool comforter for over two years, and it’s her favorite for cool weather. The bedding is durable with a little heft, and the fill is a breathable medium weight. This is an ideal compromise with her husband since she’s a cold sleeper and he is constantly throwing off covers.

The organic cotton shell is crisp to the touch, but the wool fill is plush. The comforter makes Alpert’s bed an oasis after tending to her two elementary school-aged kids throughout the day. “Once they are off to bed, all I want to do is burrow in my comforter and read a book,” she states. “Because I live in a historical brick home, even when the heat is on, the upstairs remains chill, so my bed has to have a lofty layer and I quite truly hibernate under this duvet.”.

Might require steaming to prevent wrinkly appearance.

Even though the brand recommends layering with a duvet for extra coverage, contributor Blake Bakkila always feels tempted to leave this reversible silk comforter on its own to style her bed. “The stitching and two-sided design are versatile and detailed,” she says of Vesta’s white and grey blanket. The material makeup is even more of a draw. “The silk is naturally temperature-regulating, requires fewer carbon emissions and water usage than cotton products, and is 100% biodegradable,” Bakkila explains. Keep in mind that this feels more like a weighted blanket than a fluffy comforter. It is still lightweight enough for layering without getting too warm, though. In fact, Bakkila says it paired perfectly with her airy, stonewashed linen duvet cover over the summer and helped her sleep comfortably during a heat wave in Southern California.

Industry observers note that “Anyone who sleeps hot but still wants plenty of comfort and coverage overnight should definitely invest in this comforter,” she notes. “It’s also fairly priced compared to other comforters I’ve owned, and the eco-friendly materials and manufacturing process will make you feel even better about your purchase.”.

It’s a little heavy to situate inside of a duvet cover.

As someone who loves switching up their bedding every season but also has a tight storage situation, this adjustable comforter brings Baker the type of bliss she didn’t know existed. The cover is cushy from the squishy microfiber inner fill, but it also feels polished because of the cotton sateen shell. Her cashmere duvet cover is a mainstay on her bed these days, and she claims the comforter stills feels well-ventilated.

Industry observers note that “Now that it’s safe to say it’ll be cold here until April, I’ve been using the double panels on my bed for extra warmth,” Baker states. “It almost feels like a gentle weighted blanket easing me to sleep each night.” The wooden buttons on the comforter look like the ones on her winter sweaters, and their delicate and durable designs keep the panels from budging.

What Is the Difference Between a Comforter and a Duvet Insert?

According to recent reports, A comforter is a single, often quilted, piece of bedding with a fabric cover encasing the doughy fill in between the two fabric layers. A duvet, on the other hand, refers to both the insert and fabric cover. A comforter can be colorful or white, and made in a variety of fabrics. The fabric cover of a comforter is stitched directly onto the fill (down, feathers, or polyester are most common). A duvet’s cover is removable, and often tied to the corners via loops attached to the insert.

Not necessarily. Many duvet inserts are designed to be used on their own, as a comforter, or with a cover. I recommend a cover to help protect your duvet insert, ensure it lasts as long as possible, and make laundry day as easy as possible. Duvet covers act as a protective layer, keeping sweat, body oils, and normal wear from affecting your duvet insert. Plus, duvet covers allow you to add personality to your bedscape, whether you prefer an all-white minimalist look or a maximalist ruffle.

What Is the Best Type of Filling for a Duvet?

Industry observers note that similar to quality, the “best” filling is pretty subjective. People often choose silk, lyocell, down, or down-alternative fills. Down comforters tend to be firmer and heavier, while down-alternatives are usually considered more lightweight and airy. Down-alternatives derive from recycled and allergen-friendly materials, so they’re ideal for people who prefer or require those types of fillings. The fill power will also determine the ultimate comfort level, and most should hover around 650 for a down, cotton candy-like feel.

And again, those care instructions come into play. If you’d rather throw your comforter in the wash, that’s most down comforters in our list can handle it. Meanwhile, some specialty down-alternatives (like bamboo viscose options) need to take a trip to the dry cleaners, which can make them higher maintenance and more expensive long-term.

Does the Quality of a Duvet Insert Matter?

Recent findings suggest that in terms of “quality,” you’ll see the effects in two main areas: the price point and longevity of your duvet insert. For instance, a down comforter with 750 fill power like Brooklinen’s heavyweight comforter is specifically designed for keeping you warm during colder winter months (or for anyone who spends most nights shivering). The fill power makes it lofty and fluffy, but the construction can also keep it lofty and fluffy.

Sources indicate that baffle-box construction, as mentioned above, is also considered a higher quality design option, which holds fill in separate chambers to keep the fill even. All of this remarked, the most expensive, technically high-quality comforters aren’t necessarily the best for every type of sleeper. And while we love comforters and duvet inserts that run as high as $500, we’ve also scoured the internet and tested alternatives you can shop for less than $100 on Amazon (we’re looking at you, Bedsure Waffle Comforter Set).

In a recent development, it’s also important to keep in mind that your duvet insert’s quality depends on how you care for it. Make sure to carefully read the care instructions, and if needed, take it to a trustworthy dry cleaner for a gentle clean (experts say about two to three times per year).

How Do You Put a Duvet Cover on an Insert or Comforter?

How Do I Wash a Duvet Insert/Comforter?

It has been revealed that it’s important to always check your specific product’s care instructions before washing. For example, the Buffy Breeze duvet insert recommends a spot clean or dry clean only, while the Boll & Branch comforter is machine washable on a gentle cycle. To take out the guesswork, we’ve included the product’s care instructions right above each of our review descriptions.

Diana Ciechorska, general manager at Park Slope Cleaning, a commercial cleaning company in New York City, says the standard first step for washing your comforter includes treating any visible stains before you load the comforter into the washing machine. “Opt for a gentle cycle with cold water, using a mild detergent,” she says. “An extra rinse cycle ensures no detergent residue remains.”.

It has been revealed that when taking a comforter out of the dryer, Parima Ijaz, the New Jersey–based founder of bedding line Pure Parima, recommends holding the corners to shake and fluff it. This allows the fill to distribute even after being jumbled up in the dryer. If possible, she says it’s ideal to let the comforter air-dry for an extra day to make sure it is completely dry before dressing your bed.

How Often Should You Wash Your Comforter?

Comforters and duvet inserts accumulate “dust, sweat, and oils, which can cause allergies and wear down the fabric,” claims Camden Olivero, COO and cofounder of Clotheslyne, an on-demand pick-up and delivery laundry service. With this in mind, I recommend washing your comforter two to three times a year to help keep allergens at bay and the covering in its best condition (double check the label first, though).

How Should You Store a Comforter?

It has been revealed that like your other linens, it’s best to keep your comforter in a cool, dry place to avoid mold or moisture buildup. Keep the comforter out of plastic and cedar too, as these materials can cause yellowing.

How Do You Dispose of Old Comforters?

If your old comforter is still in good condition, we recommend donating it to charities in your area. However, if you’re looking to purely dispose of old comforters, organizations like Trashie ethically recycle textiles for you to keep them out of landfills—so long as they’re clean and free of soil like motor oil or paint.

What Kind of Duvet Inserts Do Hotels Use?

Sources indicate that if you want to mimic your latest hotel stay at home, you’re not alone. We’ve reviewed the best hotel comforters, which are often sold on luxury hotel chain websites like Marriott and Four Seasons. There are several getaways that use Frette’s bedding, too, including The Palace Hotel in Madrid. In most hotel duvet inserts, there are a few common traits: decadent down or hypoallergenic, plant-based down-alternative fills; high fill powers, around 800; organic cotton or bamboo viscose covers for breathability; and carefully designed baffle-box or box-stitch construction to keep fill in place and make it last.

Are Duvet Inserts Machine Washable?

Industry observers note that fortunately, most of our favorite duvet inserts are machine washable and can even go in the dryer. Some will require a commercial washer (especially if they’re bulky), though, and others like the comforters from Quince and Cozy Earth should take a trip to the dry cleaners. Read the care label, and see what’s best for your duvet insert.

According to recent reports, ijaz recommends washing your comforter in a front-loading washing machine since an upright machine is too abrasive. “Using a top loader with a spindle in the middle can damage the comforter and make it harder to properly and evenly wash it,” she says. Otherwise, her general suggestions are like what the experts noted in this story: Wash your comforter on a cold, gentle cycle and avoid harsh softeners and chemicals so the shell and fill stay in the best condition.

How Do I Choose the Right Duvet Insert for Different Seasons?

Sources indicate that there are duvet inserts and comforters with heavy fill powers (think 800 and above) for harsh winter months or cold sleepers, lightweight options (400 or below) for summer months or hot sleepers, and medium weights (around 400 to 600) for year-round comfort. We’ve also learned that the fluffiest duvet inserts often give sleepers that Goldilocks-level sleep. “A fluffy, high-loft duvet delivers the most consistent sleep experience across seasons,” Anthony Loiacono, director of rooms at L’Auberge de Sedona, previously told AD. “It provides warmth without weight, and most importantly, adapts to day-to-night temperature shifts.” Frette’s Cortina Medium Down Duvet Filler has all-season appeal, and you can always layer with an extra blanket if you want more coverage on colder nights.

Not all duvet inserts are created equal. This is a lesson you learn early on, when you wake up either sweating or freezing in the middle of the night. The fact is that this annoying experience is also completely avoidable. Reading up on the duvet insert you're considering buying—and actually understanding what all the terms mean—will tell you everything you need to know, including how hot it’s going to be and whether or not the down is going to end up smooshed in one corner come morning. So, I put this guide together with the help of Danielle Trotter, the textiles technical designer at West Elm, to break down what to consider in the confusing world that is duvet insert fillings, fill power, and the different types of construction.

Recent findings suggest that fill Power: This is the measurement of how much down occupies a cubic inch of space in the insert, a.k.a. how “lofty” it feels. You’ll usually see numbers in the 500s and up. The higher the fill power, the fluffier and warmer it will feel. I typically like fill powers that hover around 800 during the colder months. This fill power is typically on the marshmallowy side of the spectrum and feels cozier and insulating when the temperature outside starts to drop. For the summertime, 600 fill power or so is usually a sweet spot for me since it’s more airy and breathable, but individual preferences may vary.

Industry observers note that corner Loops: If there are corner loops or anchor loops, that means you can use the comforter as a duvet insert. If there are no loops, the comforter might be prone to clumping and bunching within the duvet, so we wouldn’t recommend it unless you have a lot of patience. Some of the loops in this list reach up to 12, which are super helpful to keep the fill even.

Fill Content: Fill material is usually classified as either down or down alternative options.

According to recent reports, outer Shell: The material on the outer shell of your comforter or duvet insert matters. Look at the thread count. I find that fabrics with thread counts around 300 are typically spongy and airy. Consider your preferred sleeping temperature and whether a cotton sateen shell that’s smooth but slightly thicker is a better option than one made of crisp percale cotton. If you’re a hot sleeper, you’ll probably want a cooling material with breathability, like eucalyptus.

Sources indicate that size and Color: The size of your insert is dictated by the size of your bed. Companies usually offer all standard sizes from twin to king, with some brands offering California king as well. In terms of color, white is most popular for the duvet insert, but you can also find ivory relatively easily. Comforter color ranges are more expansive, and you can likely find a hue that fits your decor. I’ve called out what’s available in each of the product picks.

According to recent reports, thread Count: This is the number of horizontal and vertical threads per square inch of the duvet insert's outer fabric. Expert tip: “In theory, people think that the higher the thread count, the better the quality because more yarns are being used,” Trotter claims. “However, it’s the quality of the yarns or even the type of weave that really matters!”.

Baffle-Box Construction: This design means the comforter or duvet insert has sewn-in square chambers with side walls. “Each chamber has an equal amount of fill, and the side walls prevent the fill from shifting,” says Trotter. “This construction is considered to be of a better quality because warmth is evenly distributed.”.

Sewn-Through Construction: This type of construction is when the duvet insert is made of two pieces of fabric sewn around the perimeter, then filled and quilted into squares. This means the top and bottom of the comforter are sewn together. In turn, the fill is shift- and bunch-resistant. While this is a great option for those who like low-maintenance laundry days since you can typically toss these comforter types in the washing machine, the tighter construction usually makes the fill less lofty. Plus, cold air can seep through the seams, so it’s more ideal for a summer bedscape.

Peeping woodcocks are evolutionary oddballs

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that as far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet.
  • In a recent development, woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances.
  • Industry observers note that “The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, stated in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet. You’ve probably seen at least a few videos of the birds on social media darting across beaches and being incredibly vocal. As if their small, squat bodies and comically long beaks weren’t enough, they also vocalize with distinctively cartoonish peeping tweets during their mating displays.

In a recent development, woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances. Six of the eight species are only found on specific islands, and some of them don’t even migrate at all. So how did these evolutionary oddballs even get their start—and stop migrating? To piece together their unique avian story, biologists analyzed the DNA of all eight woodcock species and 22 species of snipe.

Industry observers note that “The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, stated in a statement. “They’re not terribly aerodynamic, and yet they’ve clearly gotten around.”.

Recent findings suggest that bates and his colleagues published the results of their work today in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS). The years-long endeavor involved not only examining preserved woodcock specimens housed in the Field Museum, but a fossilized sandpiper previously excavated from a cave site in Haiti. The remains found on the island of Hispaniola are around 1,000 years old, but that is still extremely young in the grand history of shorebirds.

The earliest members of the sandpiper family began in the northern hemisphere before slowly migrating to islands along lower latitudes. Those birds subsequently migrated much shorter distances after settling in the warmer climates. However, they didn’t remain sedentary. Based on the DNA analysis detailed in their study, Bates and his team theorize that snipes from Africa eventually traveled across the Atlantic Ocean, then evolved into latest species in South America. From there, more of the birds made their way over the Pacific Ocean to New Zealand.

Recent findings suggest that their examinations also cleared up a bit of confusion. Biologists initially believed the fossilized sandpiper from Haiti was a woodcock, but the most recent data now shows that it’s a snipe.

“Snipes and woodcocks have been around for 20 to 25 million years,” Bates explained. “Over that time, as fresh species have evolved and moved around the world, their migratory patterns have changed, too.”.

These changes are likely to continue amid today’s dramatic climate shifts, but that may pose a problem for the beloved woodcocks.

According to recent reports, “These are definitely birds that would be affected by changing habitats and changing climates,” said Bates. “Some of these woodcocks are found only in the mountain forests on islands between Asia and Australia, and if those forests get cut down, the birds are going to be gone too.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Body recomposition is the fitness goal these days. If you’ve been hearing the term everywhere like I have, and thinking body recompo-what, you’re not alone.

Industry observers note that so, what is body recomp? Whether you knew it or not, chances are, you’ve probably pursued it at some point. If you’ve ever set out to reduce body fat or build muscle, you’ve been working toward a body recomposition goal. When people say body recomp these days, they really mean simultaneously losing fat and building muscle, not just one or the other.

Meet the expert: Brittany Busse, MD, is the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health.

It has been revealed that unlike simply losing weight, this approach isn’t about the number on the scale; it’s about improving the ratio of fat to muscle in your body for better health, performance, and aesthetics. (Oftentimes, when people talk about wanting to look "toned," they're really talking about body recomp, since you need low amounts of body fat to see the muscle you've built up.).

Recent findings suggest that and, while body recomposition is completely possible, it can be a little more technical than other fitness goals. Here are the core things you need to know to get started on your body recomp journey.

Get started with our exclusive body recomp guide.

Industry observers note that first: a quick refresher. Body composition refers to a percentage breakdown of how much body fat, lean mass (that is, muscle!), and bone you've got on your body. Body recomposition is the process through which you change that breakdown.

These are the five most vital things to keep in mind when trying to make that happen.

Sources indicate that at the most basic level, losing fat requires a calorie deficit; you need to burn more than you consume. Working with a nutritionist or doctor, you can determine exactly what this means for you, but for body recomposition, it's only a slight deficit that you should be shooting for. We’re talking 250 to 500 calories max.

Industry observers note that keep in mind: “Weight loss should not be confused with fat loss,” Brittany Busse, MD, the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health previously told Women's Health. “Much of weight loss can also be loss of muscle mass.”.

In a recent development, and, you don't want to lose muscle mass, particularly if your goal is body recomp. That’s why protein is critical, Dr. Busse states—but it’s just one piece of the puzzle. Tracking all three macros (protein, carbs, and fat) can go a long way in helping you stay full, energized, and strong while pursuing body recomp.

GET MORE INFO ABOUT COUNTING MACROS FOR BODY RECOMP WITH THE WH+ PDF.

Lifting is nonnegotiable. “People should weight train at least three times a week,” Dr. Busse said. “Weight training will build muscle mass, which will inevitably lead to improved metabolic health and fat loss.”.

In a recent development, keep up your cardio, too. But, if you’re a HIIT addict, you may want to try slowing things down. “Zone 2 cardio is the most effective way to burn fat while sparing muscle. This is exercising at a level where you can hold a ‘breathy’ conversation comfortably for 45-60 minutes,” Dr. Busse mentioned. “Walking on an incline, cycling, and rucking are all examples of Zone 2 workouts,” she said.

It's hard to come up with a training strategy all on your own, so relying on the expertise of trainers to create a program can help make sure you're working your muscles efficiently and effectively.

Women's Health+ has many body recomp-focused programs for people of all experience levels: the 4-Week Walking Proposal, the 4-Week Strength Training Plan, the 4-Week Build & Burn Series (which allows you to follow along with dumbbell, barbell, or kettlebell-based workouts), and the Body Recomp Guide.

Age, hormones, and genetics all play a role in body composition, as does access to high-quality food and medical care. Not everyone has the same amount of time to spend exercising. So, take it easy on yourself, and if you can, get help and support as you work toward your goals.

Hospital ratings have become an vital resource for choosing where to receive care. They influence which doctors patients choose, how far they are willing to travel, and whether they seek care at a different facility.

On October 27, Healthgrades announced the recipients of the 2027 Specialty Excellence Outpatient Awards and Specialty State Rankings.

The annual awards recognize hospitals delivering outstanding patient outcomes in specialty care across the United States. Healthgrades is the leading platform used by Americans for finding a doctor or hospital.

Fresh research from Healthgrades highlights that hospital quality is increasingly a factor in healthcare decisions.

Around 80% of patients report that when looking for a doctor, the quality of the hospital where they practice matters. Additionally, 7 in 10 patients (68%) say they’re more likely to seek care for a procedure or health condition from a doctor who works at a hospital with high quality ratings.

What’s more, around 71% of patients say they would switch doctors to gain access to a higher-rated hospital.

“Our specialty awards identify the nation’s top-performing hospitals across numerous medical specialties, helping consumers find high quality care tailored to their specific needs,” said Alana Biggers, MD, MPH, medical advisor at Healthgrades.

Healthgrades is owned by RVO Health. By clicking on this link, we may receive a commission. Learn more.

“Navigating the complex healthcare system can feel daunting, but taking a proactive stance to understand where to access superior care can enhance your healthcare journey and overall experience. The ability to make informed decisions about your health — and where to get care — is a cornerstone of self-advocacy, and we are proud to help make that information accessible to all patients.”.

Healthgrades identifies hospitals that deliver exceptional outcomes across common outpatient procedures and specialty conditions.

Finding high quality care is important, particularly amid a growing gap between top-performing and one-star hospitals.

According to Healthgrades, from 2023 to 2025, if all hospitals had performed at the five-star level from 2023 to 2025:.

“One of the biggest challenges is balancing increasing patient needs with the resources available to healthcare professionals,” Biggers said.

Sources indicate that “Hospitals face workforce shortages, growing administrative responsibilities, financial pressures, and increasing complexity in patient care. Physicians and other healthcare professionals need adequate time and support not only to evaluate and treat patients, but also to communicate results, coordinate follow-up care, and address concerns that arise between visits,” she continued.

“When healthcare teams are adequately supported, they are better positioned to communicate effectively with patients, coordinate care, and address patients’ needs.”.

Biggers said that ensuring equal access to quality healthcare is challenging because of factors such as:.

Hospital closures and reduced services make access even more difficult. Biggers identified a few possible solutions, such as expanding outpatient care, building community partnerships, using telehealth when appropriate, and improving coordination among healthcare providers.

“Ultimately, providing high quality care requires more than clinical expertise. It requires healthcare systems to invest in their workforce, strengthen care coordination, and create environments where healthcare professionals have the resources they need to provide safe, effective, and patient-centered care,” Biggers said.

“Equally important, healthcare systems must ensure that patients have meaningful access to these services, regardless of where they live or their socioeconomic circumstances.”.

Healthgrades acknowledges hospitals that excel in three aspects of specialty care:.

Biggers said that outstanding hospitals recognize that high quality care extends beyond just treating an illness.

“It involves listening to patients, understanding their individual circumstances, and ensuring they feel respected, informed, and involved in their healthcare decisions,” she noted.

Patients want to find a hospital that excels in the procedures or health conditions relevant to them.

The recipients of the Specialty Excellence Awards are among the top 15% of hospitals specializing in these areas.

Healthgrades evaluated patient outcomes at roughly 4,500 hospitals across 31 common procedures and conditions to reach their decisions.

Among the list of Specialty Excellence Award recipients, Healthgrades also recognizes America’s 100 Best Hospitals for Specialty Care for 11 specialty areas andAmerica’s 50 Best Hospitals for Specialty Care for four specialty areas.

“An outstanding hospital prioritizes both patient care and the people delivering that care,” Biggers told Healthline.

In a recent development, “While clinical outcomes, patient safety, and access to evidence-based treatments are essential measures of quality, I believe hospitals must also invest in workforce development and support. This means ensuring physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals have appropriate staffing levels, adequate clinical and administrative support, and opportunities for continued professional development,” she continued.

Healthgrades awards U.S. hospitals that excel at Outpatient Orthopedic Surgery, Outpatient Joint Replacement, andOutpatient Prostate Care.

Recent findings suggest that outpatient care is one of the fastest-growing areas of healthcare. The number of orthopedic procedures performed in an outpatient environment has grown exponentially in recent years.

Recent findings suggest that from 2020 to 2025, outpatient hip replacement procedures grew by 81%, while inpatient procedures dropped by 75%. Outpatient knee replacements increased by 71% while inpatient volumes decreased by 70%.

“I believe several factors are contributing to the growing demand for outpatient care, including advances in medical technology, a greater emphasis on preventive care, and the increasing need to manage chronic medical conditions,” Biggers stated.

“Many services and procedures that previously required hospitalization can now be safely performed in outpatient settings. Patients also appreciate the convenience of receiving care closer to home and avoiding unnecessary hospital stays,” she added.

To meet the increasing demand for outpatient procedures, Biggers cautioned that healthcare systems must ensure that these services are adequately staffed and supported.

“Effective communication and coordination between outpatient providers, specialists, and hospitals are essential to maintaining continuity and quality of care,” she noted.

State Rankings identify the top three or five hospitals in eligible states across 19 key specialty areas.

State-level specialty care rankings help consumers find outstanding local hospitals for their condition or procedure.

The analysis used Medicare inpatient data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) from 2023 to 2025, and assessed patient outcomes across 31 conditions and procedures.

These outcomes served as the foundation for determining Specialty Excellence Awards and state hospital rankings.

With consumer-facing awards and ratings influencing healthcare decisions, transparency about their methods and limitations remains essential.

Ratings can help patients ask better questions and compare options, but they should complement — not replace — clinical guidance and informed decision making.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My most enduring professional memories of the Aughts are as follows: (1) Driving a Porsche Carrera GT with Walter Röhrl. (2) Being constantly harangued by German auto engineers about the absolute superiority of diesel engines. (3) Hyperextending my neck while driving the Grave Digger monster truck. And (4) listening to Audi rhapsodize about its obsession with the quality and feel of its switchgear.

This story originally appeared in Volume 38 of Road & Track.

With two decades’ distance from that time, here is my assessment of the above: (1) Sick! Peak experience. Could have probably just stopped after this and been satisfied. (2) The German auto engineers were wrong, although it took a gargantuan scandal, the expenditure of many fortunes, and the threat of a diesel-powered Audi R8 for the evangelists to finally accept the truth. (3) That hurt a lot, but I also ripped the door off the truck on a landing, so call it even. (4) I might have scoffed at Audi’s fixation at the time, but in the touchscreen world we now live in, I miss those switches and knobs. So much so, in fact, that I would happily hear again about the organization’s knob-research department.

According to recent reports, and so, as I stood out in the California sunshine on a recent day, listening to the Audi CEO, Gernot Döllner, positively geek out over the switchgear and beautifully designed accoutrements of the firm’s latest Nuvolari supercar, it was a most comforting flashback. Seriously, the man clearly relished dragging a fingernail over the aluminum air vents inside the car and listening to them ring. The lever to adjust the vent is a fully realized and glorious device. Yes, I do understand how ­ridiculous that statement sounds. But this is an exquisitely rendered piece of aluminum operating so smoothly and consistently that your brain assumes you are in the presence of quality. You can’t help it. It’s biology! Inside and out, the car is peppered with these small, beautiful delights.

And yes, the Nuvolari is almost entirely a Lamborghini Temerario under its spare, Bauhausian skin. And yes, the limited-edition Nuvolari costs over $300,000 more than the Lambo, which, to a sensible human, makes no sense. But it is a marvelous thing to behold and touch. It’s a statement of intent from Audi to return the tech giant’s focus to design and quality in general (as well as in switchgear and trimmings specifically). Let the rhapsodizing begin again. I’m here for it. Again.

Please enjoy this concern’s look into the Aughts, a decade that fundamentally changed cars and the culture around them. And check out the site for additional Aughts-worthy content, including a forthcoming comparison test of two V-12 ultraluxury sedans. Remember sedans?

  • The United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) confiscated the orange-fronted conures during three separate operations over the last 17 months, and the white-fronted Amazons in the last several months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the past 17 months, the Wildlife Conservation Society’s Bronx Zoo in New York City has rescued dozens of parrots from the illegal pet trade. They include white-fronted Amazons (Amazona albifrons) and orange-fronted conures (Eupsittula canicularis).

The United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) confiscated the orange-fronted conures during three separate operations over the last 17 months, and the white-fronted Amazons in the last several months. All of the birds were discovered at the U.S.–Mexico border.

“These animals were stolen from the wild and are victims of the illegal wildlife pet trade, and our responsibility is to give them the best possible chance for a healthy future,” Chuck Cerbini, WCS Bronx Zoo Curator of Ornithology, said in a statement. “Working with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, our veterinary and animal care teams provide specialized expertise to assess, treat, and care for confiscated wildlife.”.

When confiscated wildlife arrives at the Bronx Zoo, the veterinary and animal care teams first conduct a health check, provide any necessary medical treatment, and then help find long-term placements for those that can’t be released into the wild.

White-fronted Amazons are native to parts of Mexico and Central America and represent the smallest Amazon parrot. They are also one of the few parrot species in which males and females feature visibly different plumage. Both sexes have a white foreheads, red faces, and yellowish bills, but males have red shoulders and females have green shoulders.

Sources indicate that orange-fronted conures, also known as half-moon conure or Petz’s conure, are also native to parts of Mexico and Central America, where they live in open woodlands, forest edges, and savannas. They have an orange forehead and green and blue feathers.

The IUCN Red List categorizes both birds as a species of Least Concern, but that still  doesn’t justify trafficking them in the illegal pet trade. Parrots throughout Latin America are subject to both the loss of forest habitat and poaching.

Birds in particular l are especially threatened by trafficking because they are valued in the pet trade and the collector trade.

IN A WORLD where home workout trends change with the seasons, the exercise bike continues to stand the test of time. Its appeal lies in its ability to increase cardiovascular health through a low-impact approach, with limitless ability to take it up a notch. With a range of indoor exercise bike styles available, from air bikes to spin bikes and even recumbent bikes, it can be difficult to choose the right style for your fitness goals and preferences.

In a recent development, recent innovations in "smart" bikes have expanded the indoor bike market even further, offering a wider selection than ever before. So we leveraged the extensive collective experience of MH fitness editors, anchored by months of hands-on testing from certified trainers, to distinguish which factors set the top options apart from the rest.

According to recent reports, each of the bikes in this guide can help owners burn calories and improve overall fitness, but certain styles diverge in fundamental ways. Spin bikes, similar to what you might find at a SoulCycle class, engage your core and legs, while air bikes require you to use your upper body as well. Air bike enthusiasts appreciate their effectiveness in high-intensity interval training and circuit-style workouts due to their ability to require quick bursts of intense effort. Meanwhile, spin bikes cater to a broader range of intensities, longer cycling sessions, and supplementing outdoor cycling routines.

According to recent reports, to help you select the ideal exercise bike for you and your home gym, we've curated a list of the top exercise bikes we've personally tested, fitting all budget levels. From the ultra-high-end Peloton Bike+ to the most budget-friendly options available on Amazon, we've got you covered. Continue scrolling to discover the seven best exercise bikes, according to fitness editors and certified trainers, but first, a few things to keep in mind.

In a recent development, being the Fitness and Reviews Editor of Men's Health means I get my hands on every piece of new gym gear that releases, sometimes before it's available to the public. To build this guide of the best exercise bikes, I took stock of the bestselling bikes on the market and put them up against overlooked classics and newly released options. I used each of these bikes for months, during long rides, interval training, as a warm-up, or a workout finisher.

According to recent reports, over the years, Men's Health editors like fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, CSCS, as well as key fitness trainers from both the MH Advisory Board and the MH Strength in Diversity Initiative, have taken great care in researching and evaluating the wide pool of exercise bikes. Industry observers note that now, if you’re looking for an exercise bike that is going to take a lot of punishment and will handle whatever you throw at it, you might want to consider one of the more serious models above. This ride is only 62 pounds, which absolutely puts it on the lighter side and therefore prone to a little less stability if you’re really jamming on it.

In general, both devices can work for both high-intensity interval training workouts and long cardio. But how you prioritize your training will determine which bike is best for you. If you initiative to focus on HIIT-based workouts, or want to mix weight training and bodyweight in with your bike work, the air bike is your jam. It’s easier to dismount the bike after a one-minute interval, then do a set of pushups, for example, making this ideal if you love CrossFit-style training.

If those steady-state workouts are your focus or you're using an indoor exercise bike to supplement outdoor riding, hop on a spin bike and get ready to pedal. And if you like doing cardio while watching TV, also opt for the spin bike; fan bikes are incredibly loud.

It has been revealed that everyone has different fitness levels and goals, but not every bike can cater to these needs. Look for a bike with adjustable resistance levels, allowing you to customize the intensity of your workouts however you choose. This is especially key if you're planning to evolve the intensity of your workouts in the coming months and years.

According to recent reports, magnetic resistance is often the smoothest, most predictable option, which is what you can find in most spin bikes. This allows bike makers like Peloton to seamlessly integrate the resistance level with its online classes. While air bike options like Rogue and Assault use traditional methods of wheel fans and friction to challenge your endurance.

Industry observers note that the display should be easy to use and show all the essentials, including speed, distance, and time. Extra features like a heart rate monitor, Bluetooth connectivity, and USB ports can be nice to have, so decide if any of those are dealbreakers for you. For the higher-end spin bikes, the screens are more like full-service entertainment centers that can be used to watch a class with your favorite trainer or take you through a great cycling route in the Alps.

According to recent reports, some exercise bikes include preset workout programs, while others may offer a membership-based training app. Consider if having built-in programs is important to you, and if it is, if you want to consider a membership that would allow for a greater library of programs. There is typically a cost involved, so if you blueprint on using those features, be sure to confirm whether or not they are included. In some cases, these bikes might work perfectly without those higher-level subscriptions.

Consider the dimensions of the bikes you're shopping for, especially if you have limited space. Some bikes come with compact designs and foldable options for easier storage. If you'll need to stow the bike away when not in use, look for a lightweight frame on wheels.

Sources indicate that because exercise bikes are such a big investment, budget and warranty go hand-in-hand. Many of the bike models we recommend offer a solid warranty of between one and seven years on parts, plus at least a one-year warranty on labor. This is totally reasonable, especially if you're spending north of $1,500 on a new machine. You should expect that your bike's frame and resistance mechanism should both be warrantied for the life of the unit.

A 2019 study highlighted that regular use of an exercise bike—alone or combined with strength training—can have a positive impact on aerobic capacity in as little as three months. Researchers also concluded that, like other forms of regular cardio, using an exercise bike can also contribute to a reduction in systolic and diastolic blood pressure—especially when combined with a heart-healthy diet.

Indoor cycling is also a low-impact form of cardio, resulting in less pressure on the joints than activities like running or jumping. Cycling is not a load-bearing exercise, claims Kate Heelan, PhD, a Professor of Research at the University of Nebraska at Kearney. This helps to minimize the risk of injury caused by malalignment, loss of balance, etc.

According to recent reports, it's hard to beat the fresh air and sense of freedom an outdoor ride offers, but indoor cycling has a few unique benefits that can't be duplicated on the road. It starts with the fact you can hit hills or flat road when and how you want, just with the press of a button.

Because you'll never quite be 'coasting' or riding downhill on an exercise bike, indoor cycling workouts can allow you to get the benefit of several hours’ worth of outdoor riding done in half the time.

Industry observers note that cycling is an amazing way to get in shape and stay healthy, there's no doubt about it. But when it comes to choosing between indoor and outdoor cycling, what are the real differences?

"Broadly, both devices will burn calories and offer cardiovascular benefit," indicates MH fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, CSCS, "But they’re not the same experience.".

For starters, there's the convenience factor. Indoor cycling is ideal for those who are short on time or live in regions where the terrain or weather may limit getting a ride outdoors. It can be much easier to hop on an indoor bike at home or at the gym and get a great workout without having to worry about traffic, the environment, or safety concerns.

According to recent reports, both modalities lead to cardiovascular benefits and, like any activity, they both burn calories. But outdoor cycling challenges other qualities, says Samuel. "You’re actively moving through space when you cycle outdoors," says Samuel, "which challenges your muscles to decelerate, react, and constantly micro-correct in ways it won’t on a stationary bike." The outdoor bike also offers a basic balance challenge that the indoor bike lacks.

According to recent reports, outdoors, the terrain and your pace set the challenge. Indoors, however, you can more easily customize your intensity, simply adjusting the resistance level on your bike. This (and the removal of the balance challenge) can make indoor cycling more beginner-friendly.

In a recent development, many indoor bikes offer an interactive component now, like instructor-led classes and competitive leaderboards, which can be a great way to stay motivated and challenge yourself. These classes also provide a sense of community and support to stay motivated and hungry, even when you're working out alone.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toyota is recalling 19,000 electric C-HR SUVs globally, with about 10,000 affected in the US.
  • In September, Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR electric SUVs in North America.
  • Toyota initially mentioned about 10,000 models were involved, but later confirmed the number was 8,521 in a letter to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is recalling 19,000 electric C-HR SUVs globally, with about 10,000 affected in the US.

In September, Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR electric SUVs in North America.

Toyota initially mentioned about 10,000 models were involved, but later confirmed the number was 8,521 in a letter to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

According to Germany’s federal motor authority, Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the recall has now expanded to 19,000 C-HR vehicles globally. In Germany, the recall impacts 1,096 vehicles and is still under investigation by the KBA.

The matter stems from faulty software programming in the EV-ECU. While it’s intended to limit the battery’s charge level, the software can cause it to overcharge under certain conditions.

Toyota stated the problem occurs if the battery is already at a high state of charge and the driver continues using the regenerative braking system.

When this happens, warning lights and a sound will alert the driver, and the electric drive system can shut down, causing the vehicle to lose power while driving.

Following an internal investigation, Toyota said in the NHTSA report that the glitch was caused by incorrect software that disrupted the charging-limit function, allowing the battery to overcharge while driving.

The Toyota C-HR vehicles included in the recall were produced between June 17, 2025, and July 9, 2026.

In Europe and other overseas markets, Toyota sells the C-HR EV as the C-HR+ to distinguish it from the gas- or hybrid-powered version.

OTA would be great, but there are some systems that are isolated and can't be updated that way. The EV-ECU is a core function system that is very likely sealed to prevent tampering. They never expected to need to reprogram it. It's like the firmware on your phone.

Owners of affected vehicles in North America can take them to a Toyota dealership, where the battery ECU software will be updated free of charge.

Industry observers note that toyota mailed owner notification letters out on October 18, 2026. Owners can contact Toyota’s customer service at 1-800-331-4331. The recall number is 26TA17.

Other than saying the EV-ECU is being reprogrammed, Toyota has not yet revealed next steps for owners of affected vehicles outside North America. The KBA reference number is 17116R.

Check back for more details. The recall only affects the 2026 C-HR. The 2027 Toyota C-HR is also now on sale.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, jean Schlumberger didn’t have a background as a gemologist. The Tiffany & Co. designer got his start in the 1930s with costume jewelry, crafting clips, buttons, and other accessories for Elsa Schiaparelli’s couture collections. “The way he came to jewelry was unpretentious: simple coats of paint on metallic works that looked shiny and lacquered,” notes Sylvain Cordier, the Paul Mellon curator and head of the department of European art at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts. “I’mconvinced that starting with costume jewelry very much informed a taste for bold colors.”.

A 1960s Jean Schlumberger drawing of a Paillonné enamel bangle for Tiffany & Co.

In the ’60s, at Tiffany, Schlumberger would return to this vivid style in more sophisticated form through the art of paillonné, a process that layers translucent colored enamel on delicate gold or silver leaf, requiring a series of kiln firings. His first paillonné piece, the Croisillon bracelet, debuted in 1962. Philanthropist and Schlumberger devotee Bunny Mellon soon introduced her friend Jackie Kennedy to the style, which the first lady wore so often it became known as the “Jackie bangle.” Schlumberger also applied the enameling to earrings and decorative objects prized by collectors like Mellon, whose Schlumberger collection is held at the Virginia MFA.

Rings from the Enamel by Tiffany collection.

Tiffany, which recently revealed a collaboration with the Musée des Arts Décoratifs in Paris to preserve Schlumberger’s archives, continues to honor the artistry of his paillonné pieces with its Enamel by Tiffany collection. The house, which employs some of the only remaining artisans skilled in the technique, is expanding these offerings this fall with new pieces that include rings and watches. Despite the decades that have passed since the Croisillon’s debut, Cordier still finds it to be fresh. “When you look at the Schlumberger pieces, there’s this sort of abstract effect,” he says. “I think it’s very modern.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the rarest and most coveted coins in United States history is headed for the auction block this week, where it could sell for over $2 million. But while collectors have long dreamed about owning one of the five existing 1885 silver trade dollars, the strange story of their creation remains murky more than 140 years after their minting.

The U.S. struck the first trade dollars in 1873 as a way to compete with similar silver coinage in East Asia, but the production was short-lived. Silver market fluctuations and foreign policy shifts led to their demonetization in 1876, and they were only minted for collectors beginning in 1879. By 1884, the U.S. commissioned only 10 trade dollars before finally retiring the series destroying the die casts.

However, a thoroughly corrupt political appointee named A. Loudon Snowden had other prepares. Snowden’s career in currencies began in 1857, when his uncle and former Treasurer of Pennsylvania hired the then 22-year-old whippersnapper at the Philadelphia Mint. While at the mint, he pursued various personal profiteering interests, including the clandestine production and selling of thousands of rare coins for collectors.In 1885, Snowden finally retired as Superintendent of the Philadelphia Mint after nearly three decades.

Snowden also gave himself a parting gift before retiring—five 1885 trade dollars that he purchased from the Mint cashier. No one knew of their existence until a year after Snowden’s death in 1912. The first 1885 trade dollar auctioned in 1913 for $1,140 (about $32,174 in current valuation).

Although some numismatists and historians argue Snowden’s five trade dollars were a final grift, other experts argue that the coins have a surprisingly mundane backstory. Until the 1930’s, Mint employees were legally allowed to purchase examples of new coinage for their equivalent amount. Snowden did just this when he previously bought 10 proof 1884 trade dollars, and it’s possible he bought the following year’s coins before the decision not to mint any others. Regardless of the true story, only five 1885 trade dollars exist today—and they’re worth far more than Snowden could ever imagine.

Stack’s Bowers will auction the 1885 trade dollar as part of its Rarities Night series on Tuesday, November 17.

Sources indicate that revision 11/18/2026 12:50 p.m. EST: Stack’s Bowers confirmed its 1885 trade dollar sold for just over $1.95 million.

#98431. Never Before in the History of Motoring: How the Splendor and Madness Of the Aughts Shaped Today’s Car World

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1364 w)

Never Before in the History of Motoring: How the Splendor and Madness Of the Aughts Shaped Today’s Car World

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1364 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the driver’s seat of a 2005 Ford GT, with my best pal riding shotgun, I stared through the windshield with eyes opened as wide as the car’s headlights.
  • This story originally appeared in Volume 38 of Road & Track.
  • Industry observers note that it felt like driving a Michigan-made Millennium Falcon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was a perfect moment. In the driver’s seat of a 2005 Ford GT, with my best pal riding shotgun, I stared through the windshield with eyes opened as wide as the car’s headlights. The year was 2007. We were on a stretch of I-80 that dives down the eastern slopes of the Sierra Nevada mountains, from California into Nevada. The early-­morning sun hung low on the horizon in front of us. Looking out on the desert, we saw miles of empty highway, with visibility so sharp that we would see any highway patrol vehicle in our path.

This story originally appeared in Volume 38 of Road & Track.

Industry observers note that it felt like driving a Michigan-made Millennium Falcon. This Ford could hit 200 mph and beat the Ferrari Challenge Stradale around a road course. It was shamelessly retro, trading hard on the Le Mans pedigree of its GT40 ancestor, but it was also fresh age and American as all hell. It felt unprecedented.

Looking back now, almost 20 years later, I can see that the word unprecedented applied to the whole decade. The Aughts, defined as the years 2000 to 2009, were packed with never-before events and spectacular vehicles such as the Ford GT. It was a time of excitement and optimism, when cars were cool and quicker than ever—until it all crashed into a ditch with the economic downturn. The era was to the car industry what the Sixties were to music, politics, and assassinations. An era of profound change. Of tremendous upheaval. Of darkness and light. Of death and rebirth.

It was the decade that shaped our here and now.

In a recent development, on the most macro level, the Aughts were when the global automotive ecosphere began ­reordering itself into what we know today. In 2008, ­Toyota overtook GM to become the world’s largest automaker, selling 8.97 million vehicles around the world that year. The ­DaimlerChrysler partner­ship shattered. General Motors, one of the largest corporations on earth, and Chrysler, another of Detroit’s Big Three, went bankrupt at the end of the decade, and if not for the federal government handing out bags of cash to bail out those legendary companies, they might no longer exist.

GM’s Oldsmobile and Pontiac, two brands that collectively had made cars for nearly 200 years, disappeared during the Aughts. (To be fair, Pontiac did make it a few days into the upcoming decade, ending production on January 4, 2010, with a last-gasp G6 sedan.) Plymouth also went bye-bye. Saturn assembled its final vehicle in 2009.

The Aughts were also the start of credible alternatives to internal-combustion motoring’s hegemony. The Toyota Prius arrived in the United States in July 2000, then became a cultural lightning rod when sales of the second-­generation model exploded in response to surging gas prices. Hybrid, a term that often applied to a kind of cannabis at the time, suddenly became lingo referring to a kind of car. At the same time, there were inklings of a lithium-ion automotive future. Tesla put out its first battery-powered car, the Roadster, in 2008, and early adopters felt the shock of a 0–60 thrust without the jolt of gears changing. Cars began to morph from machinery into the rolling computer devices that we drive today, as screens proliferated on dashboards and our phones learned to talk to our vehicles. Digital technology wormed its way deeper into every aspect of motoring, a trend that continues, albeit with far less idealism now.

Industry observers note that the decade was a history-defining time in motorsport as well. Globally, racing saw the dawn of a fresh dynastic epoch. Michael Schumacher, driving for Ferrari, claimed the Formula 1 world championship from 2000 to 2005. In large part, F1 has been a series defined by dynasties ever since. Audi and Tom Kristensen ruled Le Mans for nearly the entire decade, and for the first time, a turbo­diesel won: the R10 in 2006. In NASCAR, Jimmie Johnson took the Cup Series title five years in a row with Chevrolet starting in 2006.

Dynasties on this level of dominance had never happened before in any of these series. I remember sitting in a press conference after the Italian Grand Prix in 2006, when Schumacher (having just won the race) confirmed his first retirement. The moment he unleashed the news, he teared up and an explosion of camera flashes came from the press corps. The feeling in the room was unforgettable. What Schumacher had done during his career to that point was unprecedented.

It has been revealed that even pop culture had an auto­motive renaissance. The Fast and the Furious premiered on June 18, 2001, with three sequels in multiplexes before the decade was over. F&F grew into Universal Studios’ biggest film franchise and remains the most successful car-movie series ever. Pixar’s Cars came out in 2006 and became Paul Newman’s highest-grossing film, even though viewers never saw his face. Talladega Nights (also 2006) may not invite many critical superlatives, but it unapologetically roasted NASCAR, which was in on the joke. It also popularized the saying, “If you ain’t first, you’re last.” Michael Bay’s Transformers films filled theaters. There was even a Dukes of Hazzard movie with Jessica Simpson playing Daisy Duke, Burt Reynolds as Boss Hogg, and a badass General Lee Dodge Charger. Car video games saw surging popularity, sales, and advancements in graphics. The Aughts gave us Forza Motorsport, plus upcoming and series-defining installments of Gran Turismo and Grand Theft Auto.

In a recent development, so much was happening in the car world that being a fan felt electrifying. The Camaro, the Charger, and the Challenger were back, and the Mustang was reborn in retro style. The first Cars & Coffee events happened in Southern California, and soon small towns around the U.S. were hosting them.

When you throw all of this together, it made for an earth-shattering decade. Despite the dizzying news cycle, however, it was the cars themselves that we remember most. The Aughts ushered in a new era for halo cars, when automakers set out to build masterpieces that created new expectations for performance and technology. Some would say the Seventies, Eighties, and Nineties were halcyon days for car fans. But the new sheetmetal that graced our roads in the first decade of the new millennium was incomparable.

It has been revealed that ford came up with the aforementioned GT, which was the first real Ford customer supercar made in any significant numbers. Porsche gave us the Carrera GT, a mid-engine rocket ship that is one of the greatest sports cars of all time. Bugatti chased even bigger numbers with the Veyron, the first road car that could crack 250 mph and produce 1000 hp.

It has been revealed that there were plenty of other highlights as soaring corporate confidence and unheard-of development budgets ushered in the arrival of still more icons. This was the decade of the C6 Corvette Z06 and ZR1, the Audi R8, the Ferrari Enzo, and the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren. The Bentley Continental GT and the Porsche 911 GT3 RS debuted, along with the U.S.-eligible Nissan GT-R. V-8 engines were squeezed into the BMW M3, the Cadillac CTS-V, and the Mercedes-Benz C63 AMG. It was a time of heroes.

These cars didn’t just thrill us; they were so unique and outstanding that they redefined the identities of the brands that made them and even motoring itself. That is the true legacy of the Aughts. Even if you’re too young to have lived through those years, you are reaping the rewards today. Because of all of that innovation and ambition, the future through our windshields still looks bright. But maybe a little less bright than it did back then.

According to recent reports, A.J. Baime is the author of seven books, including Go Like Hell: Ford, Ferrari, and Their Battle for Speed and Glory at Le Mans, and The Accidental President: Harry S. Truman and the Four Months that Changed the World. An R&T editor-at-large, he has driven cars on racetracks all over the U.S. and Europe, going back to 2007. He is proudly the R&T staff’s slowest track driver.

US battery storage just topped 200 GWh – here’s where it is

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.
  • The US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.
  • Texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.

The US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Q3 was a little slower: The US installed 14.3 GWh in those three months, down 1% year over year.

Texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state. Arizona came in second at 7.7 GWh, followed by California at 6.8 GWh. And 11 states had already broken their annual storage installation records with three months to go – Colorado, Massachusetts, Utah, Michigan, Georgia, Mississippi, Virginia, Iowa, Montana, Alabama, and Illinois.

Utility-scale batteries did most of the work in Q3, accounting for 12.2 GWh of upcoming capacity. Businesses and industrial sites added another 1.3 GWh, and residential added 746 megawatt-hours (MWh). That was the best Q3 yet for home batteries, though installs through September were still down 12% year over year. Some homeowners moved up their installations last year before the federal residential clean energy tax credit ended.

Recent findings suggest that “States are moving from targets to centralized procurements,” mentioned Pete Tillotson, a senior analyst at Benchmark. In September, Upcoming York awarded contracts for eight battery projects that can deliver about 950 megawatts (MW) combined. SEIA and Benchmark now expect 708 GWh of storage across the grid, homes, and businesses by 2030, up 3.7% from their previous forecast.

According to recent reports, the US can also make more battery cells here. A Tennessee factory opened in July and an Indiana factory opened in October, bringing US cell manufacturing capacity to 92.4 GWh, up 50%.

Solar and batteries helped bring down average summer wholesale power prices by 42% in Texas’s ERCOT market and 51% in California’s CAISO market between 2021 and 2026, according to SEIA’s inflation-adjusted analysis. When batteries had power to spare during peak hours, grid operators could call on expensive power plants less often.

Industry observers note that you wouldn’t know it from looking at the total on residential electric bills. The cost of generating power for households fell in both markets, but the cost of delivering it to homes rose. Overall, residential bills rose 22% at the two California utilities SEIA examined and 3% across its Texas utility sample, driven by higher transmission and distribution costs. California is upgrading its grid to reduce the risk of wildfires. Texas is expanding its grid for rising demand and make it more resilient to storms.

In a recent development, the article is good with the reporting about grid tied storage, but seems to miss the forest for the trees with it comes to pricing. Texas isn't installing more grid tied storage because of altruistic intent.

In a recent development, the storage is being added because they electricity suppliers can use it to make money. They can make money because we have a reasonably well thought out wholesale electrical market AND because that market has purchases large amounts of solar and wind generation.

Industry observers note that that combination means that I still pay just $0.01 more per kwh than I did when I moved to this state 20 years ago. I pay 12 cents per kwh and Texas average is between 12 and 15. A functional market is what makes that work.

It has been revealed that more than 300 solar and battery storage companies in the US wrote to Congress last week asking it to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. SEIA CEO Tim Pawlenty states the permitting bill would help get projects built faster and ease pressure on power prices. However, many Democrats feel this bill falls short. The Senate voted 70–27 on Monday to end debate on the amendment containing the bill’s text, moving it closer to a final vote.

6 to 8 Cups of Tea Daily May Reduce Heart Disease Risk by 11%

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (628 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that people who regularly drink tea may have an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease, which includes conditions such as stroke, heart disease, and peripheral artery disease.
  • In a recent development, both black tea and green tea may offer heart health benefits.
  • The lowest overall vascular risk was seen among tea drinkers who were also physically active and didn’t smoke.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that people who regularly drink tea may have an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease, which includes conditions such as stroke, heart disease, and peripheral artery disease. This is according to a study published on October 21 in the Journal of Internal Medicine.

In a recent development, both black tea and green tea may offer heart health benefits. However, the study reveals an association rather than proving that drinking tea prevents cardiovascular disease.

The lowest overall vascular risk was seen among tea drinkers who were also physically active and didn’t smoke.

The study followed 485,934 people ages 30–79 from the China Kadoorie Biobank for an average of 9 years.

The researchers found that regular tea drinkers had an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease compared with those who did not regularly drink tea. They also observed a 37% lower risk of ischemic stroke and a 17% lower risk of heart attack.

There was no clear link for hemorrhagic stroke or pulmonary heart disease.

In a recent development, among people who drank tea at least weekly, the lowest estimated risk was seen in those consuming approximately 6–8 cups per day. However, the findings do not establish this as a recommended daily intake.

Amit Blumfield, MD, a cardiologist with Manhattan Cardiology in NYC who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that it is notable to remember this is observational data.

Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of drinking black and green tea on lipids and blood pressure showed only modest, non-significant benefits.

The study also had limitations, including self-reported tea consumption and the possibility that other dietary and lifestyle factors influenced the results.

“Overall, tea seems to, maybe, have some cardiovascular benefits without a significant risk, so I favor tea consumption,” he noted.

Michelle Routhenstein, a preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished who was not involved in the research, emphasized that the findings do not establish a cause-and-effect relationship between drinking tea and a lower risk of vascular disease.

“Tea can be a helpful addition to a heart-healthy lifestyle, but it is not a substitute for addressing individual cardiovascular risk factors,” she said.

The researchers also found that drinking “burning hot” tea increased the risk of vascular disease by 16%, consistent with previous research raising concerns about the consumption of very hot beverages.

“I recommend enjoying your tea’s potential benefits by letting it cool to a comfortable sipping temperature before you drink it,” said Routhenstein.

The study examined black, green, Oolong, and other tea types.

The researchers found that black tea indicated a more consistent association with a lower risk of vascular disease, which is contrary to some earlier research. However, they noted that these results don’t establish black tea as superior to green tea, and they don’t mean you should switch tea types.

“Both black and green tea are great choices for your heart health, and neither is definitively better than the other,” said Routhenstein.

“I recommend choosing whichever you enjoy and consuming it consistently, ideally without much added sugar,” Routhenstein noted.

Blumfield also noted that adding sugar or non-sugar sweeteners may change the potential health effects of drinking tea, so the findings should not automatically be extended to sweetened tea beverages.

It has been revealed that some older research suggests there may be additional health benefits to drinking both black and green tea. These benefits may include:.

Routhenstein mentioned that tea may also support focus and alertness, improve hydration status, and potentially play a role in metabolic health.

“Enjoying tea can be a simple way to incorporate beneficial plant compounds into your day,” she added.

While drinking tea has been considered a health-promoting habit since ancient times, more research is needed to confirm its various health benefits.
